name: Bitwarden Secrets Manager
description: Pull API keys from Bitwarden Secrets Manager on demand instead of storing them in plaintext — one machine-account bootstrap token (BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN) replaces N provider keys, and rotating a credential is one change in the Bitwarden web app. Declarative `command` tools that shell out to the locally-installed `bws` CLI (BYO binary, no API key in the manifest).
tagline: Pull credentials from Bitwarden, not plaintext

config.description: Check that the Bitwarden Secrets Manager CLI (`bws`) is installed and report its version. Does not contact Bitwarden — no token needed. Use this FIRST to confirm the binary is present before calling the other bitwarden. tools.

List the Bitwarden Secrets Manager projects the machine account can read. Returns an array of { id, name }. Use the returned id as `project_id` for the bitwarden.list / bitwarden.get tools. Requires BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment.

List every secret in a Bitwarden Secrets Manager project. Returns an array of { id, key, value, note, projectId }. The secret `key` is the environment-variable name Bitwarden manages; the `value` is the credential itself. Use this to pull credentials on demand instead of storing them in config or env. Requires BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment.

project_id.description: The project UUID to list secrets from — the `id` returned by bitwarden.projects.

config.description: Fetch a single secret by its Bitwarden id (the `id` from bitwarden.list). Returns { id, key, value, note, projectId }. Prefer bitwarden.list when you want several secrets or do not know the id.

secret_id.description: The secret UUID — the `id` field returned by bitwarden.list.
